html:
The Sultanate of Aïr, also called the Sultanate of Agadez, was a Tuareg state in the Aïr Mountains of what is now northern Niger. The map shows it from 1715 to 1800.

Tuareg groups founded it in the early 1400s, and from about 1449 its sultans lived in the oasis town of Agadez. The sultan was usually an outsider chosen to judge between the rival Tuareg confederations, and his real power depended on them. Agadez sat on a main trans-Saharan route between the Hausa cities and North Africa, and lived from caravans, salt from Bilma and taxes on trade.

In 1501 the Songhai ruler Askia Muhammad took Agadez, and the town grew; its tall mud-brick mosque minaret dates from the 1500s. After Songhai fell in 1591 the sultanate was independent again. France conquered the region around 1900, and it became part of Niger. The sultanate still exists as a traditional office.
sum: The Sultanate of Aïr, also called the Sultanate of Agadez, was a Tuareg state in the Aïr Mountains of what is now northern Niger. The map shows it from 1715 to 1800.
